scenario: Student with an itchy rash after an unnamed antibiotic and a new soap; hives; red flags denied.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hi Neha, come in. You are a student, right? Which college?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Hi doctor. Yes, second year, at the engineering college nearby. Exams start on Monday, and now this itchy rash has come, terrible timing.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Where is the rash, and when did it start?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: On my forearms first, and now on my stomach and back also. It started maybe four days ago, no, five. I am not very sure.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Is it itchy, or painful? Do you have any fever?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Very itchy, especially at night. No fever.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any swelling of the lips or face, any trouble breathing, any sores inside the mouth?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No swelling of lips, no trouble breathing, and no sores in the mouth. Nothing like that.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Did you start any new medicine, soap, cream, or food in the last week?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Um, I had a sore throat last week, and the chemist gave me an antibiotic. I think it was azithromycin, or maybe cefixime, I do not remember. And dolo for the pain. Also I changed my soap, a new one from the hostel shop.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Do you have any known allergies?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Not really. I got a rash once as a child, I think, after some injection, but my mother never told me which one.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any skin problems before? Any asthma?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I had eczema when I was small. No asthma. My sister gets hives sometimes, I think.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me look. Your temperature is 98.6 and pulse is 76. There are raised red patches, some joined together, on both forearms, the abdomen and the back. There are no blisters, and the inside of your mouth is clear.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is it contagious? My roommate is scared and she has said she will sleep in the other room.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: No, it is not contagious. This looks like hives, an allergic skin reaction. It could be from the antibiotic, or the soap, or something else. We may never find out exactly.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What should I do about the medicines? Should I finish the antibiotic?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Please stop the antibiotic, and do not take any other antibiotic without asking me. Stop the new soap also. I will give you levocetirizine 5 milligrams at night for seven days, and calamine lotion for the itch.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Will you do any tests?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not for now. If it keeps coming back for more than six weeks, we will do a blood count and an allergy test. And please bring the antibiotic strip so I can see the name.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Is it okay to take dolo if I get fever?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, paracetamol is fine. Take cool baths, wear loose cotton clothes, and do not scratch.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Come back in one week to check the rash. But if your lips or face swell, or you feel your throat closing, come to the emergency straight away.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes doctor. Thank you.

gold.key: got a rash once as a child
had eczema when i was small
inside of your mouth is clear

notes: Exams and college small talk in turns 0 and 1 are unlabelled (the chief complaint in turn 1 is labelled). Turn 3 duration is self-corrected and hedged (four days ago, no, five, not very sure), so the key is the first phrase and it is labelled uncertain. Turn 9 names two possible antibiotics (both uncertain); the soap change is not a gold category and is unlabelled. Turn 7 is a full denial of anaphylaxis-type red flags, all labelled as negated symptoms. Turn 11 is a vague, hedged past allergy. Turn 21: the patient asks about dolo, which is a question and not a medication_history row. The doctor's return-to-emergency advice in turn 24 (lips or face swell) is hypothetical and is not a red_flag. Doctor assessment includes a negated item (not contagious) and hedged items (hives, could be from the antibiotic). Patient has taken dolo and an antibiotic; the doctor prescribes levocetirizine and calamine lotion (new) and allows paracetamol.
